explanations: luna: The section's root ب ن ي links building to the human palaces, while this verse places a built canopy over an earth made as a bed. Together they frame the human construction as something raised on God's prepared ground. | terra: God makes the earth a bed and the sky a building; this ayah reunites the spread earth and built heaven that precede the section's two uses of sewwā.
terra: فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ applies the root to ordering the heavens, extending the section's formation sense from the self to the cosmic structure.
terra: A town lies خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا and the same episode demonstrates bones being assembled and clothed; ruin and exact re-formation are placed under one power as in the section.

luna: The section names the dictionary sense of س و ي as equality and reads the leveled people as made alike. This verse calls for a كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ between communities: a shared equality of principle, which contrasts with punitive leveling that erases a people.

luna: The section names the root س و ي for leveling people; this verse uses تُسَوَّىٰ for the disbelievers' wish that the earth be leveled over them. It turns the section's imposed destruction into the condemned people's own wish. | terra: Those who rejected the messenger wish لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ; the same sewwā root turns human distinction into earth-level indistinction.
terra: Well-established generations with rain and rivers are destroyed for their sins and replaced; provision, settlement, and culpable removal form the same arc.
terra: فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا states that the last remnant of the wrongdoing people was cut off, a direct Quranic formulation of the source section's istiʾṣāl gloss.
terra: God saves Hūd and those with him while cutting off the last remnant of the deniers; this comparative judgment joins total eradication to an explicit moral distinction among people.

luna: Before Thamud hamstrings the camel, Saleh presents her as a sign and forbids harming her. This warning sets the precise act in the section against a stated boundary. | terra: Ṣāliḥ presents God's she-camel as a sign, orders that she feed on God's earth, and warns against harming her; it supplies the charged animal and ground before the first toppling.

luna: The section names the root ب ن ي for building palaces and places Thamud's palaces in the plains beside mountain-carved homes. This verse gives both forms of settlement that the leveling of the people reverses. | terra: Ṣāliḥ names both sides of Thamūd's terrain: palaces on its plains and houses carved from mountains, the raised works the section sees reduced to the plane beneath them.

luna: The section's root ع ق ر is the camel-hamstringing that precedes the people's leveling; this verse says they hamstrung the she-camel, supplying that precise deed in its narrative context. | terra: Thamūd hamstring the she-camel, عَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ, and defiantly demand punishment; this is the first toppling from which the section reads their own toppling.

luna: The section describes the people leveled after building on the plain; this verse leaves Thamud جاثمين in their homes, giving the bodily result of that leveling. | terra: After the quake, Thamūd lie جَاثِمِينَ in their own dwelling: the narrative itself shows the people pressed down where their built life stood.

luna: Like Thamud in 7:78, the deniers of Shuʿayb end جاثمين in their homes after an earthquake. The repeated bodily and domestic aftermath clarifies that the section's laying-flat scene is a Quranic judgment pattern. | terra: The quake leaves Midian جَاثِمِينَ in their home, a repeated Quranic formula for communal collapse within the inhabited center.
luna: This verse says Shuʿayb's deniers seem never to have lived there, echoing the disappearance stated of Thamud in 11:68 and making the emptied settlement a repeated aftermath.

luna: This verse pairs the destruction of Pharaoh's people's buildings with the structures they had raised. It gives a specific build-then-destroy parallel to the section's palaces and mountain homes followed by Thamud's leveling. | terra: God destroys what Pharaoh and his people manufactured and what they raised on trellises; constructed and cultivated works are brought down together.
terra: God makes the mountain دَكًّا and Moses falls down stunned; mountain and person together enact the section's linked senses of leveling and being struck to earth.

terra: The man who could have been raised instead أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ, clinging downward to earth; that moral lowering gives a Quranic counterpart to the source section's dictionary sense of settling heavily toward the ground.

terra: The rebuke asks why the hearers اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ, became heavy toward the earth; this exactly realizes the source section's dictionary gloss for the earth-root branch rather than merely repeating its noun.
terra: A building on a crumbling bank collapses with its builder; the ayah turns construction itself into a fall and contrasts it with the sound foundation named earlier in the verse.

luna: This verse pictures flourishing vegetation becoming harvested as though it had not flourished the previous day. It parallels the section's dry-stalk aftermath and Thamud's homes seeming never inhabited.
terra: Ṣāliḥ says God produced Thamūd from the earth and settled them in it; their earth-derived, earth-building life sharpens their final reduction to that ground.

luna: Saleh commands his people to leave God's camel grazing in God's earth and not harm her. This is the explicit boundary that their hamstringing in 11:65 and the section's destruction cross. | terra: Ṣāliḥ calls her God's she-camel and warns that harm will bring near punishment, making explicit the causal symmetry developed by the section.

luna: The section names ع ق ر for the camel's hamstringing before the people are struck down. This verse narrates that same act and its three-day warning. | terra: فَعَقَرُوهَا repeats the communal hamstringing and gives the three-day limit, setting the camel's fall directly before the people's destruction.

luna: Before the blast leaves Thamud prostrate in 11:67, this verse says Saleh and the believers with him were saved. That survivor boundary qualifies the section's image of the community being leveled. | terra: When the command comes, God saves Ṣāliḥ and those who believe with him; this sets the moral boundary around 11:67-68's communal leveling.

luna: This verse likewise leaves Thamud in their homes after the blast. Its fallen-in-place scene makes the section's account of the community being laid flat tangible. | terra: The blast seizes Thamūd's wrongdoers and leaves them جَاثِمِينَ in their homes, the same bodily ground-state highlighted through 7:78.

luna: The section says Thamud's settlement is erased by the leveling; this verse says their homes look as though they had never lived there, showing what remains after the people are gone. | terra: كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا makes Thamūd's settled presence disappear as though they had never inhabited the place, completing the section's image of a civilization erased to ground.
terra: God makes the top of Lot's towns their bottom; the literal reversal of high and low is a close companion to reducing raised habitation to ground.
terra: The blast leaves Shuʿayb's wrongdoers جَاثِمِينَ in their homes, confirming that the posture developed in the section is a recurring image of judgment.
luna: This verse applies the same “as though they had never lived there” aftermath to Madyan that 11:68 gives for Thamud; it sharpens the section's image of a people erased from their settlement.
terra: Among the judged towns, some remain standing and some are حَصِيدٌ, mown down; the contrast directly renders settlements either upright or reduced like a reaped field.
terra: God does not destroy towns unjustly while their people are reformers; this is a direct boundary on the section's image of an entire settlement leveled for sin.

luna: This verse describes the earth as spread and then names its provisions. It recalls the section's plain as a prepared human dwelling-place before Thamud's settlement is erased. | terra: God extends the earth and sets mountains and rivers upon it; this differentiates the plane and its raised features before the leveling image removes such distinction.

luna: The section treats the spread earth as the prior surface of the leveling; this verse says the earth was spread and set firm, a direct counterpart to the later contourless plain. | terra: God spreads the earth and places firm mountains in it; the pairing of extension with height supplies the very topography later turned into an unbroken plane.
terra: God says فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ before breathing spirit into the human; the same root denotes the completed bodily forming that stands behind the section's proportioned self.
terra: The decree concerning Lot's people is that their last remnant will be cut off by morning; it is another precise Quranic formulation of root-and-branch eradication.
terra: The overturned towns have their highest part made lowest, another direct scene in which built elevation is divinely inverted.

luna: This verse identifies the people of al-Hijr as deniers of the messengers, the people whose secure mountain-cut homes appear in 15:82. It anchors those dwellings in the Thamud story developed by the section. | terra: The residents of al-Ḥijr deny the messengers; this identifies the stance of the very rock-house dwellers whose security and overthrow 15:82-83 stage.

luna: The section links carved dwellings to a people who thought they were secure; this verse says they carved mountain homes while آمنين, making the collapse of built refuge concrete. | terra: They carved houses from mountains ءَامِنِينَ; their felt security inside elevated stone is precisely what the section's ruin scene overturns.

luna: After the secure mountain homes in 15:82, this verse says the cry seized their people at daybreak. It supplies the destruction that reverses the security described in the linked verse. | terra: The cry takes the rock-house dwellers in the morning; after 15:82's claim of security, this ayah performs the sudden overthrow.
terra: What the rock-house dwellers had earned avails them nothing after the cry, naming the failure of accumulated works to resist leveling.
luna: This verse says mountains were set in the earth lest it sway with people. The section shows mountain homes and then a leveling that removes the terrain, a reversal of this stabilizing role.
terra: God attacks a building from its foundations and its roof falls upon its occupants; raised shelter becoming the agent of collapse closely matches the fate of Thamūd's refuges.
terra: A town's affluent people rebel and the town is destroyed utterly; culpability within inhabited prosperity leads to total demolition just as sin leads to Thamūd's leveling.
terra: The she-camel is given to Thamūd as a visible sign and they wrong her; the ayah isolates the sign whose violation the section makes the hinge of reciprocal overthrow.
terra: The believer reminds his companion that God created him from dust and a drop, then سَوَّاكَ رَجُلًا; the root marks a person brought to finished form.
terra: The proud garden may become صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا, bare slippery ground; flourishing possession is reduced to a plane just as Thamūd's constructed landscape is leveled.
terra: The garden's produce is destroyed and its trellises lie خَاوِيَةً عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا; it supplies the collapsed built scene whose final ground-state 18:40 anticipates.

luna: The section compares the destroyed Thamud to dry plant debris; this verse uses هَشِيمًا for vegetation reduced to dry fragments, while its parable shows how quickly a flourishing scene disappears.

luna: This verse says the mountains are set moving and the earth made exposed. It extends the section's mountain-to-level-land image into the judgment scene. | terra: Mountains are removed, earth stands exposed, and no person is left out of the gathering; the ayah joins a bare plane to the section's concern with nobody being set apart.
terra: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ الصَّدَفَيْنِ uses the s-w-y root while building an elevated barrier level with the two cliffs; 18:98 then reverses that construction into leveling.

terra: The immense barrier becomes دَكَّاءَ when God's promise comes; a divinely enabled construction is made level by the same Lord, a close structural parallel to the image's two works of one power.

luna: The section's root س و ي describes a soul brought into proportion; this verse uses سَوِيًّا for the human form in which the angel appears to Mary. It is another concrete instance of the root naming a fully formed human figure. | terra: The messenger appears as بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا, a well-formed human; this distinct Quranic use of the root illuminates the section's "properly formed" branch.

luna: This verse calls the earth a cradle and lays paths through it. It makes the section's stretched ground a provision for dwelling before human settlements are leveled. | terra: God makes the earth a cradle and lays paths through it; its fitted habitability supplies the constructive face of the ground later leveled in the same surah.

luna: The question about the mountains introduces the removal that leaves a plain in 20:106–107. Its own contribution is to make the mountains, also the place of Thamud's homes, the thing removed before leveling. | terra: The question concerns the mountains and the answer says God will scatter them completely; it identifies what God turns into the level field described in 20:106-107.

luna: The section's flattened people are set against the spread ground; here the mountains are removed and the land is left قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا, making a level surface the scene of judgment. | terra: God leaves the mountains قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا, the bare level plain that most directly matches the section's account of a people made into flat ground.

luna: This continuation specifies that the leveled land has no عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا, an exact contourless landscape for the section's image of leveling. | terra: The level field of 20:106 has neither bend nor rise; this ayah supplies the visible content of the section's "none set apart" reading of leveling.
terra: Later people walk through the dwellings of generations God destroyed; remaining houses become evidence of inhabitants removed.
terra: God saves those He wills and destroys the excessive; the paired outcomes clarify that one power does not entail an undifferentiated moral fate.
terra: God says many wrongdoing towns were قَصَمْنَا, shattered, and another people raised after them; communal breaking and replacement closely express the section's eradication sense.
terra: The doomed townspeople are told to return to their luxury and dwellings; this identifies the inhabited prosperity that 21:15 turns into a reaped, extinguished community.
terra: A wrongdoing town is made حَصِيدًا خَامِدِينَ, reaped and extinguished; the harvest image closely parallels Thamūd as crushed enclosure-straw.
terra: God rolls up the sky and promises to repeat creation as He began it; cosmic unmaking and exact re-creation are expressly works of the same agent.
terra: Wrongdoing towns become خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا beside an abandoned well and a lofty palace; ruin, habitation, and the high building meet exactly as in the section.
terra: The blast rightfully seizes the wrongdoers and makes them غُثَاءً, washed-up debris; a whole people is reduced to discarded matter as Thamūd is to crushed straw.
terra: Thamūd are explicitly included among successive peoples who rejected, placing their fate in a wider series of demolished communities.
terra: Each of those peoples received clarifying examples and each was destroyed completely; the ayah supplies the totalizing end of the Thamūd-inclusive list in 25:38.
terra: ʿĀd build a monument on every height in play; the elevated building supplies a comparative scene of a powerful people investing in conspicuous height.
terra: They take great structures as though they might live forever; the imagined permanence directly contrasts with a built people being erased.
terra: ʿĀd deny their messenger and are destroyed, completing the construction-to-destruction comparison opened by 26:128-129.
terra: The question "Will you be left secure in what is here?" exposes the permanence assumed by the people who carve enduring homes.
terra: Thamūd's secure setting includes gardens and springs; this is part of the inhabited abundance within which 26:149's mountain houses seem permanent.
terra: Crops and laden palms further specify the cultivated plain surrounding Thamūd's carved houses, sharpening what is lost when the people are seized.

luna: The section's mountain-house image is stated again of Thamud here: they carve dwellings in the mountains, so the later flattening reaches a people who made homes in rock. | terra: They carve mountain houses with skill or exultation; this close parallel to 15:82 adds human confidence and craft to the structures later unable to save them.

luna: In the passage leading to the hamstringing, this verse assigns the she-camel a drinking turn. It completes the camel scene behind the section's mention of her injury. | terra: The camel has her allotted drink and the people theirs; the measured sharing makes her violation a concrete breach rather than an incidental animal death.

luna: This verse warns Thamud not to touch the she-camel with harm after her assigned drink. It states the boundary violated in the next verse's hamstringing. | terra: Ṣāliḥ warns them not to touch her with harm lest a tremendous day's punishment seize them; 26:157-158 carry that warned reversal out.

luna: This verse says Thamud hamstrung the she-camel, the exact deed named through the section's root ع ق ر before their destruction. | terra: فَعَقَرُوهَا makes the camel's hamstringing the immediate act for which the people become regretful and are seized, preserving the section's two-stage fall.

luna: After the hamstringing in 26:157, this verse says the punishment seized them. It completes the section's sequence from the camel's injury to the community's leveling. | terra: The punishment seizes them immediately after the camel is hamstrung, completing the section's causal passage from the animal's fall to the people's.
terra: God states أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ; total destruction of the plotters and their people directly expresses the section's eradication and collective leveling.

luna: The section moves from Thamud's elevated and carved homes to their destruction; this verse calls their houses خَاوِيَةً because of their wrongdoing, showing the settlement emptied and collapsed. | terra: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً بِمَا ظَلَمُوا points to their emptied, fallen houses and expressly ties the ruin to wrongdoing, just as the section ties leveling to sin.
terra: After the houses stand empty, God saves those who believed and were mindful; the ayah prevents "all made one" from erasing the distinction made within the same Thamūd account.
terra: Mountains that appear fixed pass like clouds, while the ayah names this the workmanship of God who perfected everything; stable height and exact workmanship meet in one divine act.
terra: Pharaoh orders a lofty structure built so that he can challenge Moses' God; elevated construction becomes a concrete expression of the pride answered in 28:40.
terra: God seizes Pharaoh and his forces and casts them into the sea, completing the movement from the self-exalting tower of 28:38 to collective overthrow.

luna: This verse describes destroyed prosperous towns whose dwellings remain scarcely inhabited. It parallels the section's empty, collapsed homes and people seeming never to have lived in their settlement. | terra: Self-indulgent towns are destroyed and their dwellings remain scarcely inhabited, paralleling the section's civilization reduced to empty habitation.

luna: The people of Madyan are seized by the earthquake and left in their homes, paralleling Thamud's prostrate bodies in the section and its cited 7:78. | terra: Midian's denial brings the quake and leaves them جَاثِمِينَ in their dwelling, repeating outside the Thamūd story the exact posture of a people struck to ground.
terra: ʿĀd and Thamūd are named, and their dwellings remain evident to the audience after their deeds led them away; surviving habitation makes the absent peoples' overthrow visible.
terra: Each destroyed people is seized for its sin by storm, blast, earth, or flood; the ayah expressly unites culpability with differing divine acts of bringing societies down.
terra: Earlier peoples worked and developed the earth more powerfully, yet wronged themselves after messengers came; built abundance therefore gives no immunity from the moral cause of ruin.
terra: ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ describes God's proportioning of the human before breathing spirit into him, directly paralleling the section's fashioned self.
terra: The destruction of earlier generations whose dwellings are still traversed makes ruined habitation an admonitory sign, as Thamūd's houses are in the section.
terra: A single cry leaves the town خَامِدُونَ, joining one decisive sound to collective stillness as in the accounts of Thamūd.
terra: The audience is asked how many generations were destroyed before them and told those peoples do not return; this supplies the irreversible communal absence following the single cry.
luna: Where the section says the punished people could not rise, this verse has the dead rise from graves and hasten to their Lord, making resurrection the pointed reversal of their fallen posture.

luna: The denier asks who can revive bones after decay; this is the destruction-and-restoration question that 36:79 answers and that the section's shaped fingertip invokes. | terra: The denier presents decayed bones and forgets his own creation; his objection gives the resurrection-denial setting behind the section's fingertip example.

luna: This verse answers that God revives the bones by recalling their first creation. It links the section's fine divine shaping to God's power after bodily ruin. | terra: The answer says the one who originated the bones first will revive them, explicitly joining original formation to re-formation after destruction.
terra: The repeated creation formula فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ again joins exact human fashioning with the divine breath, confirming this formative use of s-w-y.
terra: Former peoples were stronger and left greater traces in the earth, but God seized them for their sins; this closely restates monumental power followed by culpable erasure.
terra: The earth is a settled place, the sky a structure, and human forms are made beautiful; all three elements of the section's created plane, building, and fitted person occur together.
terra: On the earth God fixes mountains, blesses it, measures its provisions, and makes them سَوَاءً for those who ask; the root's equality sense appears within an ordered earthly landscape.
terra: Thamūd choose blindness after guidance and are seized by a humiliating thunderbolt because of what they earned, preserving both culpability and communal ruin.
terra: Believers who were mindful are saved from the thunderbolt of 41:17, explicitly separating them from the culpable community brought low.
terra: The earth appears humbled and lifeless, then stirs and grows when water descends; the same ground-state that resembles leveling becomes evidence that the giver of life can raise the dead.

luna: This verse also describes the earth as a cradle with paths. It gives a habitable, prepared surface as the prior condition to the section's flattened settlement. | terra: God makes the earth a cradle and places ways within it, another scene of the ground deliberately fitted before human building.
terra: The evildoers ask whether God will make them سَوَاءً with believers in life and death; this denied equality marks the limit of the section's equality-through-destruction reading.
terra: The wind leaves nothing visible of ʿĀd except their dwellings; the surviving buildings form a precise counter-scene to Thamūd's houses themselves shown empty and ruined.
terra: A people more firmly established than the addressees lose the benefit of hearing, sight, and hearts when they reject God's signs; establishment cannot prevent disappearance.
terra: Travelers are told to see the predecessors' end: God destroyed what was over them; the wording makes ruin descend upon a formerly established people and their world.

luna: This verse again describes the earth as spread with mountains set upon it. It supplies the created terrain against which the section's mountain-cut homes and final leveling are read. | terra: The earth is spread and firm mountains cast into it, another direct formulation of the extended ground presupposed by the section.
terra: Stronger generations ranged through lands seeking escape, yet found none; strength and reach fail as refuge just as Thamūd's stone works do.
luna: The section leaves Thamud unable to rise; here the earth splits open and the dead hurry out to their Lord. The contrast shows the final rising that follows the prostrate state.
terra: The passage identifies ʿĀd and the barren wind sent against them, supplying the agent whose reducing action 51:42 describes.
terra: The barren wind leaves whatever it reaches كَالرَّمِيمِ, decayed remains; it supplies another Quranic scene of destruction reducing a people and their world to spent material.
terra: Thamūd are told to enjoy themselves only for a time; the bounded respite prepares the rebellion and collapse of 51:44-45.
terra: They rebel against their Lord's command and the thunderbolt takes them while they look on; it supplies the blow whose bodily result is the inability to stand in 51:45.

luna: The section names Thamud's inability to rise after the punishment. This verse states that they could not manage قيام, the bodily opposite of the formed and standing human. | terra: They cannot rise and cannot help themselves after 51:44; inability to stand renders the secondary tahā sense of being struck and stretched on the ground.
luna: The section's named root ب ن ي is used here of God's building the heaven. That gives the human construction in the section a direct Quranic counterpart under the same root.

luna: The section's image begins from the earth spread out before the people are laid flat; this verse describes the earth as spread, making the habitable ground itself part of the parallel. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا presents God as the one who spread the earth, matching the speaker and act behind the section's prior plane.
terra: The mountains move away completely, another Quranic dissolution of the elevated landscape.
terra: وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَىٰ says that no remainder of Thamūd was left, the clearest Quranic statement behind the section's "none separately spared" sense.
terra: God casts down the overturned towns, a compact scene of habitation and people made to fall from high to low.
terra: The wind uproots people as though they were trunks of uprooted palms; bodily felling and eradication parallel the section's joined senses of collapse and istiʾṣāl.
terra: Thamūd deny the warnings; the ayah identifies the collective stance answered by the camel test and single cry later in the passage.

luna: This verse presents the she-camel as a trial for Thamud just before the water-sharing instruction and hamstringing. It supplies the test that makes the section's named act culpable. | terra: God sends the camel as a test and commands watchful patience; this frames the act of hamstringing as the decisive communal trial.

luna: The camel's water is divided between her and the people before they hamstring her in 54:29. This verse gives the specific shared resource and boundary behind the section's act. | terra: Water is divided and each drinking turn attended; this supplies the measured order that the act in 54:29 breaks.

luna: The section's root ع ق ر names the decisive blow against the camel; this verse states that the people hamstrung her, immediately before the punishment arrives. | terra: One companion undertakes the act, فَعَقَرَ, while the ensuing punishment reaches the people; this sharpens the section's movement from one assailant to a community made one in consequence.
terra: The question "How were My punishment and warnings?" makes divine warning and consequence the explicit bridge between the single hamstringer in 54:29 and the community's reduction in 54:31.

luna: The section cites the image of Thamud becoming dry crushed plant matter; this verse says they became هَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ, carrying the same specific dry-stalk aftermath. | terra: The single cry makes them كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ, crushed enclosure-straw; it is the Quran's most concrete analogue for the section's people spread flat like a trampled field.
terra: The earth is shaken violently; this opens the sequence in which its mountains are pulverized and become scattered dust in 56:5-6.
terra: The mountains are ground to powder, a direct enactment of raised mass losing every stable height before 56:6 disperses it.
terra: The pulverized mountains become scattered dust, the final material state of the leveling begun in 56:4-5.
luna: This verse's worldly-life crop yellows and becomes debris. It connects the section's dry remains to a Quranic image of what flourishes only to be brought down.

terra: People think their fortresses will protect them, but their houses are demolished by their own hands and the believers'; this makes explicit the failed refuge implicit in Thamūd's secure rock houses.

luna: This verse says God created people, made their forms good, and to Him is the return. It joins the section's formed-human image to the return after the leveling of a people. | terra: God creates the heavens and earth and makes human forms beautiful; cosmic construction and finished human form again belong to the same agent.
terra: The layered heavens show no تَفَاوُت, no disparity in the Merciful's creation; this states in other words the fitted, non-disjointed order conveyed by formative sewwā.
terra: The owners' fruitful garden becomes like a field cut down overnight; cultivated abundance is abruptly reduced to a reaped surface.
terra: Thamūd and ʿĀd deny the Striking Calamity; it gives the shared act of rejection whose distinct bodily destructions follow.
terra: Thamūd are destroyed بِالطَّاغِيَةِ; the concise communal end names the same people and the overwhelming force that brings them low.
terra: ʿĀd are destroyed by a furious, violent wind; this ayah identifies the force that leaves the bodies fallen like hollow trunks in 69:7.
terra: The people of ʿĀd lie fallen like hollow palm trunks, a bodily landscape parallel to Thamūd left prostrate on their own ground.
terra: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ asks whether any remnant remains after 69:7, reinforcing the section's reading of totality rather than individual distinction.
terra: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً; their heights become one under a single blow, matching both flatness and equality in the section.
terra: Mountains become like dyed wool, carrying the same reversal from weight and height to dispersed fiber.

luna: The section reads the spread earth as the surface later leveled; this verse says God made the earth a بساط, a laid-out expanse for people. | terra: God makes the earth a carpet for humankind; the usable expanse parallels the open flat-land sense attached to ṭaḥā.
terra: Earth and mountains convulse and the mountains become a heap of loose sand; stable height collapses toward the section's level-ground end.

luna: The question immediately before the fingertip verse asks whether human bones can be gathered. It supplies the resurrection problem to which 75:4 answers by asserting God's power even over the fingertips.

luna: The section pairs God's shaping of the soul with the leveling of Thamud as acts of one power. This verse says He can نُسَوِّيَ بنانه, restore even the fingertips, making the small-scale shaping an explicit counterpart to destruction. | terra: نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ uses the same root for the exact re-forming of fingertips, making explicit the section's claim that minute formation and annihilating leveling belong to one power.
terra: From the clot God creates and فَسَوَّىٰ; within the same surah as the fingertip promise, the root again denotes exact human formation.
terra: After recalling human creation and proportioning, the passage asks whether that maker can revive the dead; it states the power inference the section draws from exact formation.
terra: God created people and strengthened their frame, yet can replace them at will; bodily construction and removal are explicitly held together under one power.
terra: The mountains are blown away, removing the raised features that distinguish the landscape from a plain.

luna: By calling the earth a مهاد, this verse presents the ground as a laid-out habitation, the stable surface that the section shows becoming an even plain. | terra: The earth is made a resting spread, a compact parallel to the section's prepared level ground.
terra: The mountains are set moving and become a mirage, turning apparent solidity into absence.
luna: The section includes بَنَىٰهَا and the lexicon's building sense; this verse says God built the heaven, setting divine construction alongside the human palaces whose builders are later leveled.

luna: The verse between heaven's construction and earth's spreading describes the heaven as raised and proportioned; it continues the section's linked images of divine building, shaping, and the ground below. | terra: God raises the sky's vault and فَسَوَّاهَا; the same root fashions the sky whose building stands beside the fashioned self in the surah's oaths.

luna: After the heaven is built in the same passage, this verse says the earth was spread. It recalls the section's spread ground as the setting on which human structures rise and can be leveled. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا depicts the earth spread out, a close nonlexical parallel to ṭaḥāhā as an open plane.
terra: The mountains are set in motion, an eschatological removal of the heights that structure ordinary ground.

luna: The section's named root س و ي first describes a soul formed in proportion. This verse uses فَسَوَّىٰكَ for God's proportioning of the human being, grounding the same shaping action elsewhere in the Quran. | terra: خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ joins creation, proportioning, and balance; it states directly the formative and equalizing face of the root used for the soul in the section.

luna: After saying God formed the human, this verse says He assembled him in whichever image He willed. It extends the section's formed-human side of the contrast with Thamud being laid flat. | terra: After 82:7's creating, proportioning, and balancing, this ayah says God assembled the person in whatever form He willed; it contributes the particular configuration produced by formative sewwā.

luna: The section's spread ground is later made level; this verse says the earth is extended, مُدَّتْ, at the end, turning the same ground into an eschatological scene. | terra: At the end the earth is مُدَّتْ, stretched out; created extension becomes an eschatological scene of the plane, matching the section's movement from preparation to leveling.

luna: Following the earth's extension in 84:3, this verse says it casts out what is within it and becomes empty. That completes the section's image of a surface left after the people and their dwellings are gone.

luna: The section connects سَوَّى to bringing a being into due form; this verse uses فَسَوَّىٰ in the same divine act of creation and proportioning. | terra: الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ makes creating and proportioning one divine act, a terse parallel to the formative sewwāhā side of the image.

luna: The section treats the spread earth as the prior form of leveling; this verse asks how the earth was سُطِحَتْ, directly presenting its spread, even surface. | terra: The command to look at how the earth سُطِحَتْ presents the prepared flat surface that the section treats as the prior form of later leveling.

luna: The section cites the root ط ح و for flat terrain and the rock-cut Thamud. This verse identifies Thamud as those who cut rock in the valley, joining the people to the landform later leveled. | terra: Thamūd جَابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ, cutting rock in the valley; this is the monumental mountain-building that gives their later leveling its force.
terra: The monumental peoples just named, including Thamūd, are identified as those who transgressed in the lands; the ayah supplies the shared cause of their fall.
terra: Those same peoples multiplied corruption in the lands, extending the causal account from impressive building to destructive conduct.

luna: After 89:9 names Thamud's rock-cutting in the valley, this verse says the Lord poured punishment on the transgressing peoples named in the passage. It supplies the consequence for the ruinous landscape described there. | terra: The Lord pours upon the named peoples a scourge of punishment, completing the sequence that begins with Thamūd's rock-cut landscape in 89:9.

luna: The section cites Thamud's rock-cut valley in 89:9; later in the same surah the earth is دُكَّتْ دَكًّا, pounded flat. The same landscape of human carving is answered by the ground itself being leveled. | terra: دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا stages the earth itself being pounded flat, a direct nonlexical formulation of fe-sewwāhā.

luna: This verse says the human was created in the best stature, a nonlexical parallel to the section's balanced, formed soul before its contrasting account of people laid flat. | terra: Humanity is created فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ, a nonlexical parallel to the self being brought into a sound, balanced form.
luna: After the best stature in 95:4, this verse describes the descent to the lowest state. It gives a specific form-to-lowering reversal like the section's passage from proportioning to leveling.
luna: This verse pictures the earth itself shaken at the end. It extends the section's earthly leveling from punished bodies and dwellings to the ground that moves beneath them.
luna: This verse says the earth brings out its burdens, a related judgment image to the section's fallen people and the extended earth that casts out what is within it in 84:3–4.

luna: This verse makes the mountains become fluffed wool on the Day of Judgment. It adds another explicit Quranic scene of the terrain being undone before the section's flat plain. | terra: Mountains become like fluffed wool, a material unmaking comparable to the section's hard-built world reduced to loose remains.
terra: The army is made like eaten straw, a compact parallel to Thamūd's reduction to crushed enclosure-straw in 54:31.
